b: I like to think of this as the Bon Jovi prompt day. Because after today, we’ll be halfway there (livin’ on a prayer).

For today’s prompt, take the phrase “(blank) End,” replace the blanks with a new word or phrase, make the new phrase the title of your poem, and then, write your poem. Possible titles might include: “Dead End,” “Until the Very End,” “A Poem Before the End,” and/or “Halfway to the End.” I’ll also accept variants that use -end at the end of another word with examples like: “And Now We’ll Descend,” “All the Light Will Bend,” “Fences We Can Mend,” and/or “A Castle to Defend.”
Remember: These prompts are springboards to creativity. Use them to expand your possibilities, not limit them.

Here’s my attempt at a Blank End Poem:

I don’t think I will find the end,
though I’m sure the end will find me
searching for meanings to defend;
but what will I find in the end,
and what messages will I send
that matter to eternity?
No, I don’t think I’ll find the end,
though I’m sure the end will find me.
